newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo stocks finish sharply lower, turnover modest.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo stocks finish sharply lower, turnover modest.

text.p: Tokyo stocks finished sharply lower on Wednesday, battered psychologically by news that a regional bank had said it suspects a former employee misused bank funds, brokers said.
Selling linked to stock futures also depressed the market, they said.
The cash market's key Nikkei 225 average tumbled 276.41 points, or 1.32 percent, to end at 20,681.67. In the futures market, the key December futures contract fell 250 points to finish at 20,690.
"The market was in a wait-and-see mood, foreign investors were net sellers and then news of financial trouble at a bank emerged to depress the market further," one broker said.
Earlier on Wednesday, Biwako Bank Ltd said it suspects a former employee of the bank improperly used bank funds worth about 3.4 billion yen ($29.8 million).
Biwako did not yet know how much of the 3.4 billion yen ($29.8 million) it would be able to recover, so the size of the bank's losses from this was not yet clear, a bank official said.
Earlier, Biwako said the incident was not a financial problem for the bank. ($1=114 yen)
